svg.title: Telemetry firmware data flow
svg.desc: Hardware sources feed priority-ordered interrupt and DMA handlers, which push timestamped data through static queues to decoder tasks, a 10 Hz record builder and a log writer that targets two microSD slots.
svg.text: Telemetry firmware: data flow and task priorities
Rust, no_std, bare-metal. RTIC schedules everything by interrupt priority. No heap, no RTOS. P4 is the highest priority.
EXTI then SPI DMA FIFO read
map PPS capture to GPS time
tel-core fusion: newest value per source
LEDs, watchdog, card state, USB console
SPI2: PB2, PB14, PB15, CS PB0
SWO PB3 and RTT via J2 / J12
Rules that keep it deterministic and memory safe
1. Every buffer and queue is statically sized at compile time, so there is no allocation at run time.
2. Interrupt handlers only timestamp and enqueue. All parsing happens in lower priority tasks.
3. Logic lives in no_std crates with forbid(unsafe_code), unit-tested on the PC.
Only the HAL drivers and the RTIC macros contain unsafe.
4. Both CAN controllers use bus monitoring mode, so the logger cannot disturb the car's networks.
5. A queue overrun increments a counter that is written into the next record.
